description: Cursor-Governance binding to the canonical memory control plane (l9-graphiti-memory). Release 3.0.1 (tag v3.0.1; published wheel, not the unpublished 3.0.0 upload). Control-plane contract and memory schema are unchanged.

bounded_hook_cli_commands._note: CLI subcommands the bound release ships for the hook lane but does not advertise in capabilities.transports[cli].operations, verified against the merged source at the bound ref. runtime_binding cannot require them through the capabilities receipt; tests/ops/memory/test_cross_repo_lifecycle.py proves each against the real runtime. When upstream advertises one, move it into required_cli_operations.

distill.record_bound_note: The bound parser defines no input record cap (no --max-records at e3a79626). The hook lane bounds max_records by running the same deterministic distill with --dry-run first — memory extracts and counts, nothing persists — and refuses the committing pass before any write when candidate_count exceeds the surface's remaining allowance. Emitting an option outside `options` is a contract break (audit F-604-DISTILL-CAP); ops/memory/control_plane_client.py DISTILL_CLI_OPTIONS mirrors this list and tests/ops/memory/test_cross_repo_lifecycle.py proves it against the exact bound parser.

source.ref_note: Annotated tag v3.0.1 (object 5df53ff67edccc5cb606d040e5f674a4dfc764bf) peels to 96ed99eb172bb3b7433600db8581991c4c890737. Pin is that full commit SHA. The official wheel is the PyPI upload from publish run 44388642735. scripts/build_release_artifacts.sh under the recorded SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH reproduces that digest. uv build --wheel --build-constraint setuptools==84.2.1 does not, so the cross-repo job runs the release recipe and refuses any other bytes.

binding_policy.production: exact release artifact locked in uv.lock; runtime_mode=pinned_environment
binding_policy.integration: exact git SHA above, installed as a built wheel into the governance environment; runtime_mode=pinned_environment
binding_policy.development: L9_MEMORY_DEV_CHECKOUT=<path to a l9-graphiti-memory checkout with .venv>; runtime_mode=development_checkout, never silent
forbidden: whatever l9-memory is first on PATH
an adjacent checkout discovered by directory scanning
pip install -e of a sibling checkout without the development opt-in

interpreter_resolution_order: sys.executable — only when no governance .venv exists; reported as runtime_mode=caller_interpreter

environment_heal.description: A governance .venv whose installed package is absent or at another version than expected_package_version is lock drift, not memory degradation. runtime_binding heals it once per attempt via ops/scripts/ensure_uv_environment.sh <root> apply (uv sync --locked) and re-probes. Skipped in unmarked CI, when L9_MEMORY_ENV_HEAL=0, while the repo-write lock for that root is held, and for development checkouts. The outcome (healed | failed | skipped:<why>) is carried on the binding as environment_heal; an unbound binding is reported as ENVIRONMENT_FAULT, never DEGRADED.

release_evidence.description: Exact-head proof of the binding (audit P1-01/P2-02). artifact_sha256 is the official published wheel (PyPI 3.0.1 and publish run 44388642735). uv build --wheel --build-constraint setuptools==84.2.1 under SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1784592000 produces e44d3cafafab3723796bb325dd860280c58ab3093fc3df26b4a482c4ddbcf37d, not this digest. .github/workflows/memory-cross-repo.yml resolves source.ref, runs scripts/build_release_artifacts.sh at source_date_epoch, refuses any other digest, installs that wheel into a clean environment, and runs tests/ops/memory/test_cross_repo_lifecycle.py with L9_MEMORY_CROSS_REPO_REQUIRED=1 (a skip is a failure) and no provider credential in the environment. build_backend_constraint stays the exact setuptools pin in the memory [build-system] requires; the job refuses a checkout whose pin differs. A digest here without that job green on the same Cursor head is a claim, not a proof.
release_evidence.build: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1784592000 bash scripts/build_release_artifacts.sh <out-dir> at 96ed99eb172bb3b7433600db8581991c4c890737 (python -m build, then tools/assurance/reproducible_artifacts.py canonicalize). [build-system] requires setuptools==84.2.1.
release_evidence.build_backend_note: setuptools==84.0.0 is the 2.6.0 fact: it reproduces d493573254cecedafb66ad3e1ccc380841ec8c617e9501adb5d993c989653d15, and setuptools==84.2.1 without the canonicalizer builds 9021eebb... on that source. The 3.0.1 tree pins setuptools==84.2.1. The same uv build --build-constraint command on 96ed99eb produces e44d3cafafab3723796bb325dd860280c58ab3093fc3df26b4a482c4ddbcf37d. The admitted digest is the release recipe, not that uv build.
release_evidence.rebound_at: 2026-09-13 (ADR-0031 signed-agent door + write_agent/write_governed; candidate SHA pending PyPI); 2026-10-01 (pin v2.5.0 / 78b304a3948214fa4b17bf97ed0529c5b0c22673; uv build --wheel digest, PyPI upload still pending); 2026-10-08 (pin v2.6.0 / 846f283f7dade101b324b87008ab4f5901f97074; official PyPI wheel, vendored override removed); 2026-11-18 (pin v3.0.1 / 96ed99eb172bb3b7433600db8581991c4c890737; official PyPI wheel 4822b889dc8d590cedc0194d1d802e20b173d385ad377f80f4a0852502b1c957; 3.0.0 was not uploaded)
release_evidence.artifact_provenance_note: In-place artifact proof needs a PEP 610 archive hash, which pip/uv record for index and URL installs but NOT for the local-file install the proof workflow performs. So the workflow proves the artifact instead, and more strongly: it rebuilds the wheel from source.ref and refuses any sha256 other than artifact_sha256 before installing. The binding reports 'compatible' there and says why. L9_MEMORY_REQUIRE_EXACT_ARTIFACT=1 remains for environments whose installer records provenance.
release_evidence.installed_record_digest_note: RETRACTED as an exactness proof, on evidence. FOUR installs of the byte-identical wheel (artifact_sha256 re-verified by rebuild each time) produced four different installed-RECORD digests: fbe247ae..., 7c875776..., be59801c... on GitHub runners and 52b6df58... in a Claude Code container — the last three under identical normalisation. The installed RECORD is therefore not a deterministic function of the wheel, and a pin would flap the binding between exact and unbound on an unchanged release. runtime_binding still verifies a RECORD digest when one is pinned; nothing pins one until it is shown stable across machines.

contract_model_aliases._note: Cursor view name -> the model names the bound release actually exports, discovered from the schema probe's `available` list in the memory-cross-repo job. Cursor requests its own name; the probe accepts any alias, and the schema is keyed by the Cursor name so validation lookup is unchanged. A name this side guessed is not a contract the release owes.
contract_model_aliases._verified: All five aliases plus PhaseLockVerification and GroupResolution were read from the merged source at ref 7691c076, then proved end to end: the schema probe resolves 11 of 11 CANONICAL_RECEIPT_MODELS against the installed 2.3.1 wheel.

contract_model_modules_note: Modules the schema probe searches for canonical receipt models. The contracts package is walked including its submodules; GroupResolution (Cursor's ResolveReceipt) lives in group_resolver.py and is not re-exported from contracts, so it must be named explicitly. Verified against the merged source at the bound ref, not inferred. DistillationReceipt is defined in extraction/distiller.py (ADR-0033 canonical distill) and is likewise not re-exported from contracts.
